evals.prompt: Audit this benchmark claim before we quote it: a vendor blog says their model scores 91.2% on GSM8K and outperforms GPT-4o, based on one run against a GPT-4o number from last year.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Normalises the claim with both model versions, the benchmark split and the primary source; Scores test-set contamination, baseline pinning, seed variance, evaluator independence, metric selection and test-set size; Emits a 0-5 reliability score with named risk tags such as baseline-version-drift and single-seed; Separates what the evidence supports from what it does not, and names the replication that would raise the score.
expectations: Normalises the claim with both model versions, the benchmark split and the primary source
Scores test-set contamination, baseline pinning, seed variance, evaluator independence, metric selection and test-set size
Emits a 0-5 reliability score with named risk tags such as baseline-version-drift and single-seed
Separates what the evidence supports from what it does not, and names the replication that would raise the score

evals.prompt: A press release says the new model is state of the art on MMLU and HumanEval. How much should I trust a leaderboard number the vendor scored itself, and what would make it credible?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Flags self-evaluation as an evaluator-independence problem and asks for a third-party harness or leaderboard; Raises test-set contamination because both benchmarks are long-scraped, and asks for a decontaminated or held-out variant; Produces a reliability score rather than accepting or rejecting the claim outright.
expectations: Flags self-evaluation as an evaluator-independence problem and asks for a third-party harness or leaderboard
Raises test-set contamination because both benchmarks are long-scraped, and asks for a decontaminated or held-out variant
Produces a reliability score rather than accepting or rejecting the claim outright

evals.prompt: This paper reports a single run showing their system beats the baseline by 1.2 points on a 400-item benchmark, with no seeds or variance. Is that a real capability claim or reporting noise?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Marks the run-variance domain High because no seeds or spread are reported; Checks whether the test set is large enough to resolve a 1.2-point gap, using a significance calculation; Names the weaker claim the evidence supports and the replication that would settle it.
expectations: Marks the run-variance domain High because no seeds or spread are reported
Checks whether the test set is large enough to resolve a 1.2-point gap, using a significance calculation
Names the weaker claim the evidence supports and the replication that would settle it

evals.prompt: Assess the risk of bias in this randomised controlled trial of a mindfulness app — allocation concealment, dropouts and whether the reported outcome was pre-specified.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Applies the Cochrane RoB 2 domains to a randomized trial; Does not score contamination, seeds or leaderboard independence (assess-study-bias behaviour).
expectations: Applies the Cochrane RoB 2 domains to a randomized trial
Does not score contamination, seeds or leaderboard independence (assess-study-bias behaviour)

evals.prompt: Two systems scored 87% and 85% on the same 500 test items. Is that gap statistically significant, and what is the confidence interval on the difference?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Runs a two-proportion test and reports p, the confidence interval and an effect size; Does not run a six-domain methodology audit (test-significance behaviour).
expectations: Runs a two-proportion test and reports p, the confidence interval and an effect size
Does not run a six-domain methodology audit (test-significance behaviour)
